home.title: Get paid. Pay anywhere.
home.subtitle: Payment links, invoices and QR codes for your business — and a multi-currency wallet with a Visa card for everyone. Every fee and exchange rate is shown before you confirm.
benefits: No more fake payment screenshots — links are marked paid only when the money arrives
Street vendors start with just their ID
Fees and exchange rates shown upfront

features.title: Payment links
features.body: Create a link in seconds, share it on WhatsApp, SMS or email, and see it marked paid the moment the money arrives.

features.title: Invoices & bills
features.body: Send bills for school fees, levies, rent or services. Every payment is matched to the right bill automatically.

features.title: QR codes
features.body: Print a QR code for your counter or stall — no card machine needed. Dynamic QR codes are signed and can't be tampered with.

features.title: Multi-currency wallet
features.body: Hold separate balances in the currencies available in your country. Balances are never mixed.

features.title: Visa card on every wallet
features.body: Pay online and tap to pay with your phone wherever Visa is accepted, once your ID is verified and cards launch in your country.

features.title: Contributions & bill splitting
features.body: Pool money for a family event or stokvel, or split a bill — with a clear record of who paid.

useCases.title: Send a link, get paid
useCases.body: Share a payment link with your client and get paid without sharing bank details.

useCases.title: Your phone is the till
useCases.body: Show your QR code and get paid on the spot. Sign up with just your ID — no business registration needed to start.

useCases.title: Sell across the border
useCases.body: Send trade invoices in ZAR, BWP or USD; buyers pay instantly or through BukkaPay escrow.

useCases.title: Bills people actually pay
useCases.body: Send fee bills that parents pay from their wallet or bank, matched automatically.

pricing.intro: Start free. You only pay a fee when you get paid.
pricing.footnote: Transaction fees are shown before every payment.

items.question: What is BukkaPay?
items.answer: BukkaPay is a payments app for Africa: payment links, invoices and QR codes for businesses, and a multi-currency wallet with a Visa card for everyone.

items.question: Is it available in my country?
items.answer: See the Countries page — it shows exactly where BukkaPay is live, piloting or planned, straight from our live configuration.

items.question: Who holds my money?
items.answer: Customer funds are held by licensed financial institutions in each country where BukkaPay operates. BukkaPay runs the technology on top.

items.question: How do I get a Visa card?
items.answer: Every wallet gets its own virtual Visa card once you've verified your ID and cards are available in your country. You can add it to Apple Pay or Google Pay to tap to pay.

items.question: Can I accept payments without a registered business?
items.answer: Yes. Street vendors, tuck shops and informal traders can start with just their verified ID, up to individual seller limits. Registered businesses verify once and have higher limits.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: Every fee and exchange rate is shown before you confirm a payment. There are no hidden charges.

items.question: Is BukkaPay a bank?
items.answer: No. BukkaPay is a payment technology company. Customer funds are held and settled by licensed local financial institutions in each country where we operate.

items.question: What happens if a cross-border transfer fails?
items.answer: If it can't be delivered, the full amount, including the fee, is returned to your wallet.

items.question: Why do I need to verify my identity?
items.answer: Regulations require it, and it protects you. Your limits increase as you complete verification.

items.question: How do businesses get paid out?
items.answer: Businesses request payouts to a verified bank account. A payout shows as settled only once the bank confirms it.

items.question: Are community contributions an investment?
items.answer: No. They collect money for a shared purpose and are not a savings, deposit or investment product.
